questions.q: What are the four deep work strategies Newport describes?
a: Monastic, bimodal, rhythmic and journalistic
Morning, evening, weekend and seasonal
Solo, paired, group and public
Planned, unplanned, timed and flexible
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the four approaches, from total isolation to seizing odd free moments.

a: A fixed multi-hour block for deep work, then everything else
Working in short bursts throughout the entire day
Never doing any deep work on weekends
Alternating between two different offices each week
questions.why: Lesson 1 says bimodal sets aside a long block and leaves the rest of the day free.

a: Thinking through a hard problem during otherwise unproductive time
Sitting quietly and clearing the mind of all thoughts
Writing down every idea that arrives during a walk
Meditating before work to improve concentration
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests using commutes, showers and chores to work on a complex problem.

questions.q: Why should you stop working at the same time every day?
a: The brain needs free space to wind down and recover
Deep work only produces results in the morning
Clients stop sending emails after normal hours
It makes it easier to skip planning the next day
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a fixed stopping time protects you from burning out.

questions.q: What should be your first step when choosing a deep work strategy?
a: Track how you currently spend your time
Buy a calendar and fill it with meetings
Ask a colleague which method they prefer
Eliminate all breaks from your schedule
questions.why: Lesson 1 says monitoring your time reveals productive and unproductive patterns.
